questions.question: What is a checking account primarily designed to support?
choices: Ownership of a company's stock
Long-term government borrowing only
Insurance against every investment loss
Deposits and routine payments

questions.question: What is a savings account generally used for?
choices: Holding money while often earning interest
Borrowing money without repayment
Buying voting rights in a corporation
Trading only foreign currency

questions.question: What is interest on a loan?
choices: The amount of the original principal only
A refund of every banking fee
A charge for borrowing money
A payment that cancels the loan automatically

questions.question: What is loan principal?
choices: The lender's annual advertising budget
The amount borrowed before interest charges
The interest charged each month
The borrower's total lifetime income

questions.question: What is a debit card generally linked to?
choices: Funds in a deposit account
A separate investment ownership share
A guarantee of unlimited borrowing
A government retirement benefit

questions.question: What is a certificate of deposit generally associated with?
choices: Owning part of a publicly traded company
Receiving a loan with no repayment schedule
Paying for insurance against medical expenses
Depositing money for a stated term under specified conditions

questions.question: What institution insures eligible deposits at FDIC-insured banks?
choices: Securities and Exchange Commission
Internal Revenue Service
Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
Department of Education

questions.question: How do banks connect savers and borrowers?
choices: They store only coins and never lend
They accept deposits and provide loans and related services
They convert every deposit into a stock purchase for the depositor
They determine all national wages directly

questions.question: Why should account holders review fees?
choices: Charges can reduce balances or offset interest earned
Every account has identical fee rules
Fees are unrelated to banking costs
Banks must refund every fee automatically

questions.question: Why might a bank charge an overdraft fee?
choices: The account holder receives too much interest
The bank sells stock to another investor
The borrower finishes repaying a loan
A covered transaction may exceed the available balance under account terms

questions.question: How does compound interest differ from simple interest?
choices: Compound interest applies only to the original principal
Simple interest requires changing the principal every day
Compound interest includes interest on previously earned interest
Simple interest always produces more growth at the same positive rate

questions.question: Why can a CD be less flexible than a basic savings account?
choices: CDs always permit unlimited penalty-free withdrawals
Early withdrawal may involve penalties or other restrictions
CDs are necessarily uninsured stock investments
Savings accounts must be closed after one deposit

questions.question: Why is a bank statement useful?
choices: It helps track transactions, balances, and possible errors
It guarantees that future prices cannot rise
It replaces every receipt for every purpose
It determines the customer's citizenship status

questions.question: What does deposit insurance not generally cover?
choices: Eligible checking deposits within coverage rules
Eligible savings deposits within coverage rules
Eligible CDs within coverage rules
Losses in stock investments

questions.question: Why do lenders evaluate a borrower's ability to repay?
choices: They must give every applicant identical loan terms
A borrower's income has no relationship to repayment
They assess the risk of nonpayment
Loan applications determine election eligibility

questions.question: An account begins with $200, receives a $75 deposit, and pays $40, with no fees. What is the ending balance?
A $1,000 deposit earns 4% simple interest for one year with no fees. How much interest is earned?
A person uses a debit card for a purchase. What generally happens?
choices: A share of the merchant's stock is issued
The government pays the purchase as a grant
The account earns interest equal to the purchase price
Money is drawn from the linked deposit account

questions.question: Two accounts pay the same interest rate, but one has higher fees. What comparison is most relevant?
choices: Only the bank's building size
Only the account's advertising colors
Net earnings and costs under each account's terms
Only the number of letters in the bank's name

questions.question: A customer notices a duplicate withdrawal on a statement. What financial skill does this situation call for?
choices: Assuming all statement entries are automatically correct
Reconciling records and investigating the discrepancy
Treating a withdrawal as new income
Calculating a stock's dividend yield
